lessons.title: subtle
lessons.meaning: Not obvious; requiring attention to notice.
lessons.example: There is a subtle difference in tone between those replies.
lessons.notes: Use this pattern when the meaning fits the situation. Practice both a neutral tone and a warmer, conversational tone.
lessons.conversation:
A: Could you give me an example of how you would say that?
B: There is a subtle difference in tone between those replies.
lessons.exercise: Make this your own: write one example from your life, then say it aloud without reading. Notice stress, tone, and how the phrase fits the context.

lessons.title: Confidence grows when practice becomes a habit.
lessons.meaning: Regular repetition builds ease over time.
lessons.example: I kept this reflection in mind while deciding how to respond.
lessons.notes: Use this reflection to encourage consistent practice. Becomes a habit means an action grows familiar through repetition; avoid presenting confidence as an immediate result.
lessons.conversation:
A: What idea are you reflecting on today?
B: Confidence grows when practice becomes a habit.
lessons.exercise: Make this your own: write one example from your life, then say it aloud without reading. Notice stress, tone, and how the phrase fits the context.
